source_policy: Primary references support definitions and stated conditions. Scenarios and worked derivations are originally authored constructions. The supplied book matrix guides sequencing; it is not independent verification of exact-edition book coverage.
purpose: Connect an arrival rate to count probabilities while retaining the undisplayed tail.
meaning: A Poisson distribution assigns probabilities to nonnegative counts using a nonnegative mean. A homogeneous Poisson-process interpretation assumes constant rate and independent increments. For positive mean, infinitely many counts are possible.

definition.setting: A return-slot model counts arrivals in one minute with mean λ. The homogeneous Poisson-process interpretation assumes independent increments and a constant rate. Inspect the count distribution rather than inventing a simulated arrival history.

signature.λ: Expected arrivals in a fixed minute.

conditions: A return-slot model counts arrivals in one minute with mean λ. The homogeneous Poisson-process interpretation assumes independent increments and a constant rate. Inspect the count distribution rather than inventing a simulated arrival history.

The Poisson distribution has infinite support. Geometry displays counts 0–20 and a separately stated remaining probability; the displayed bars are never renormalized. At λ=0, zero arrivals are certain. Real arrival streams need model validation.
